A lot of MGS gameplay and level design are based on the camera. MGS in first person would, for starters, need to have completely redone, generic controls. First person stealth games are awesome, but it just wouldn't be MGS. If you seriously haven't played any FPP stealth yet, check out:

  • Call of Cthulhu: Dark Corners of the Earth, if you don't mind (a little, to be honest) horror thrown in

  • Penumbra series, same as above, just actually scary

  • Now that I think about it, first person survival horror seems to pretty much always rely on stealth - so games like Amnesia and Outlast

  • Deus Ex series

  • Thief series, just not the new one, it's shit

  • Dishonored if you don't mind killing (a non-lethal playthrough of that one is one of the most boring things I played through)

  • Hitman has a first person mode (not sure if each one has it; I know BM for sure does) and it's quite fun even if less convenient than staring at 47's back all the time

Here are some sources for learning I have found helpful:

Youtube:

  • Nick Sibicky - Geared toward double digit kyu and some single digit kyu. Always good stuff in his lectures and games.

  • Dwyrin - Lots of Go content. Great lectures, entertaining games, and commentary on pro and amateur games.

  • Haylee - Hajin LEE - Professional player and International Go Federation General Secretary. Comments on games while she plays. Something for all levels of players here.

  • Andrew Jackson - Teaches single digit kyu classes in Seattle. Some very good content.

  • Josh Lee - Lots of great lectures. Not much new content recently, but what's there is very good.

  • Little Lamb Go - Has commented games and a few lectures. His lectures on openings are quite good.

  • Shawn Ray - Game reviews and lectures.

  • Songbirdo - A single digit kyu. Does lots of commentary on his own games. Has a series on "Get Strong at ..." books. I understand that he has worked out the copyright concerns with the author/publisher.

  • An Younggil - 8 Dan Pro! Great lectures.

Twitch

  • Twitch Go Channel - Keep an eye out here for live games. Several Youtube content creators stream on twitch.

Teachers

  • Yunguseng - In-seong Hwang's online go school. Lots of videos, live lectures, and a league with reviewed games.

  • Kaz - Kaz is a former Go insei and Tokyo regional Igo representative. Great teacher.

There are so many more, but this is a good starting point.

Books

I don't have a lot of books, but here are a few I find helpful. I'm sure other people have more suggestions.

  • Essential Life and Death Series
  • Get Strong at Invading
  • Get Strong at Attacking
  • Whole Board Thinking in Joseki
  • The Workshop Lectures - Yilun Yang

The GOP May Regret Its Lasting Battle Against Gay Marriage

Unfortunately, this may turn out not to be the case. Something Chief Justice Roberts said in the Obergefell case struck me as particularly apt:

There will be consequences to shutting down the political process on an issue of such profound public significance. Closing debate tends to close minds. People denied a voice are less likely to accept the ruling of a court on an issue that does not seem to be the sort of thing courts usually decide. As a thoughtful commentator observed about another issue, “The political process was moving . . . , not swiftly enough for advocates of quick, complete change, but majoritarian institutions were listening and acting. Heavy-handed judicial intervention was difficult to justify and appears to have provoked, not resolved, conflict.” Ginsburg, Some Thoughts on Autonomy and Equality in Relation to Roe v. Wade , 63 N. C. L. Rev. 375, 385–386 (1985) (footnote omitted). Indeed, however heartened the proponents of same-sex marriage might be on this day, it is worth acknowledging what they have lost, and lost forever: the opportunity to win the true acceptance that comes from persuading their fellow citizens of the justice of their cause. And they lose this just when the winds of change were freshening at their backs.

I support gay marriage rights, but I fear he may be right that the decision did more harm than good. We may be looking at another abortion: an issue that looked like it would end up forever in the past, kept alive by the frustration of a people who never had the chance to make the choice themselves.

an issue that looked like it would end up forever in the past, kept alive by the frustration of a people who never had the chance to make the choice themselves

Yep. I've always been a fan of gradual change and peaceful persuasion to change culture, not using the force of government. It may be a slower process but I believe it's more thorough and results in less violence.

Yes preventing free association of individuals is wrong but the way in which this was implemented may backfire extremely. The civil war didn't solve the problems of racism (and may have made it worse), Roe v. Wade didn't solve issues surrounding abortion, and I don't think this solved anything relating to freedom of association and could possibly lead to worse issues when it comes to that topic.
